conceptual assets.information: The accumulated processor-cycle count used for cycle accounting and performance observation. It is loaded, incremented, and returned through the CSR readback interface.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The cycle count can reveal execution timing and is exposed through the cycle counter readback and rdata_o at lines 136, 347-349, and 97. The CSR write data can overwrite the counter through lines 133-135 and the counter storage assignments at lines 302-305 and 325-329. The cpu_debug and cnt_halt controls can suppress counting through cnt_en at lines 108 and 131, producing an incorrect count if used outside the intended debug or halt behavior.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to issue an unauthorized CSR read or write, or assert the debug or halt controls, could disclose, overwrite, or suppress the cycle count.

conceptual assets.information: The accumulated number of retired instructions used for instruction-count accounting and performance observation. It is loaded, incremented, and returned through the CSR readback interface.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The instruction-retired count can reveal execution behavior and is exposed through the instret readback and rdata_o at lines 155, 347-349, and 97. CSR write data can overwrite it through lines 152-154 and the counter storage assignments at lines 302-305 and 325-329. The cpu_debug and cnt_halt controls can suppress instruction counting through cnt_en at lines 110 and 150, producing an incorrect count if used outside the intended debug or halt behavior.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to issue an unauthorized CSR read or write, or assert the debug or halt controls, could disclose, overwrite, or suppress the instruction-retired count.

conceptual assets.information: The per-event hardware performance-monitoring counts used to measure selected processor events. The counts are stored in the counter instances and combined into the CSR readback value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Hardware event counts can reveal workload and execution behavior and are exposed through hpm_read_back and rdata_o at lines 190, 222, 227, and 97. CSR write data can overwrite the HPM counters through lines 187-189 and the counter storage assignments at lines 302-305 and 325-329. The event, debug, and halt inputs control HPM increments through lines 112 and 185, so unauthorized use can make the reported measurements incorrect.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to read or write the HPM CSRs, change event-selection settings, or assert debug or halt controls could disclose workload activity or falsify the performance measurements.

conceptual assets.information: The stored per-counter event selectors that determine which processor events increment the HPM counters. The configuration is written through CSR data and can be returned through CSR readback.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The event selectors are mutable configuration state: cfg_we selects the write and csr_wdata is stored in hpmevent at lines 199-200, with reset and forced-field behavior at lines 196-197 and 202.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to perform an unauthorized CSR write could select the wrong events or disable intended HPM measurements.

considered, not kept.concept: Counter update event, halt, and debug gating
considered, not kept.reason: These inputs only determine the increment pulse that paces or suppresses counter updates at lines 108-112, so the pacing-pulse and processor-context rules fold them into the counter values rather than making them independent assets.
csr_addr, csr_re, and csr_we only specify whether, where, and in which direction a register access occurs at lines 82-86 and 90-94, so the access-command-fields rule bars them as independent pieces.
time_rd is assigned only all-zero constants at lines 140, 164, and 237, so it contains no meaningful information whose confidentiality, integrity, or availability requires protection.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the counter and configuration state through lines 102-106, 129-130, 148-149, and 183-184, and the clock/reset rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
